title: Sintropic Sovereignty: 10mm Diamond-Sapphire Chip on 127-Qubit Hardware
abstract: This research addresses the fundamental challenge of maintaining biological homeostasis and genomic stability under extreme radiation environments (100 TeV) and microgravity conditions, common in deep-space colonization scenarios such as Project Helios. We propose a paradigm shift from traditional entropic biological models to a Quantum Biocybernetics approach, utilizing highdimensional F-Theory manifolds (12D) to govern matter-information interactions. The central thesis involves the deployment of a synthetic CVD-Diamond/Sapphire micro-processor acting as a sintropic controller over 127-qubit IBM Transmon hardware. Our results, validated through 10,000 Monte Carlo cycles, demonstrate a manifold fidelity of 99.9500% and a real residual error of 0.0500%, maintaining a Sub-Hartree precision limit of 1.0μHa. The calculated Sintropic Index (ΔS = −7.6009) confirms that the system effectively reverses entropic decay, ensuring scale invariance from the atomic level to macro-biological structures. This study provides the first irrefutable technical evidence of Atomic Sovereignty, where quantum mechanotransduction is used to preserve DNA integrity against ionizating radiation. The architecture presented herein represents an 80.0x benchmark superiority over standard 3D computational paradigms, establishing a new frontier for aerospace engineering and long-duration spaceflight survival.

title: Fidelity-Aware Channel Allocation in Quantum Repeater Networks using Recursive and Clustered QAOA
abstract: Quantum repeater networks(QRN) require efficient resource allocation to maintain highentanglement fidelity under noise and interference. We formulate this problem as a physicsinformedquadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) and solve it using the QuantumApproximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). To enable scalability on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices, we introduce a cluster-based variant (CLQAOA) that decomposesthe global problem into smaller subproblems. We compare CLQAOA with classicalmethods, including Greedy and Simulated Annealing, and observe that it achieves nearoptimalsolution quality with controlled runtime scaling. We further incorporate RecursiveQAOA (RQAOA), which improves solution quality through iterative variable reduction butincurs higher computational cost. These results demonstrate that hybrid, cluster-basedquantum optimization provides a practical pathway for scalable quantum repeater networkcontrol, balancing solution quality and computational efficiency.

title: La inteligencia artificial en redes sociales sobre el comercio electrónico juvenil en Dolores Hidalgo, C.I.N., Guanajuato
abstract: El estudio analizó la influencia de la inteligencia artificial en la personalización del comercio electrónico en jóvenes de 18 a 26 años de Dolores Hidalgo C.I.N., Guanajuato, mediante un enfoque cuantitativo, descriptivo y no experimental con 346 participantes.Los resultados evidencian diferencias de género: el 58% de los hombres muestran mayor frecuencia y confianza en el uso de Inteligencia Artificial, mientras que el 42% de las mujeres presentan menor familiaridad y seguridad.Estas diferencias parecen estar relacionadas con factores culturales y estereotipos de género.Los hallazgos subrayan la necesidad de fomentar una alfabetización digital más equitativa.

title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks
abstract: Two strong transformative fields in contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) are quantum computing and deep learning. Neuro-nanophotonic systems also introduce quantum-inspired innovations that enhance the computing power of neural networks. Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks (QINNs) have shown promise as a potential alternative to the classical deep learning models, particularly when processing high-dimensional data and solving complex problems efficiently. QINNs leverage the attributes of quantum mechanics to enable efficient deep learning methodologies, achieving superior performance in AI-based applications. In this research, we present a QINN framework that synergizes the power of Quantum Variational Circuits (QVCs) and Quantum Natural Gradient Descent (QNGD) to improve learning efficiency of learning. Experimental results show that QINNs can achieve 97% accuracy, which is 4.5% improvement over the classical models, and computational time and energy consumption can be reduced by 45% and 53%, respectively. Furthermore, QINNs exhibited greater robustness to adversarial noise, making them better candidates for healthcare, cybersecurity, and large-scale AI applications. The results illuminate the game-changing ability of QINNs with respect to scalable, cross-computational and highly resilient AI architectures.

title: Data Clustering Method for Fault‐Tolerant Privacy Protection of Smart Grid Based on BGN Homomorphic Encryption Algorithm
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the issues of lengthy encryption time, low clustering accuracy, and poor performance in existing privacy‐preserving clustering methods for grid data, this paper proposes a fault‐tolerant data clustering method for smart grids based on the Boneh‐Goh‐Nissim (BGN) homomorphic encryption algorithm. A system architecture is constructed comprising a cloud server layer, a fog node layer, a smart meter layer, and a trusted third party. Private data collected by smart meters are first denoised using robust locally weighted regression. The preprocessed data are then encrypted with the BGN algorithm. K‐means clustering is applied to mine valuable data, with decryption performed at the cloud server layer. A two‐layer fault‐tolerant mechanism—utilizing secure channels to trusted organizations—is implemented across both the cloud servers and smart meters to ensure robust privacy‐preserving clustering. Experimental results in a scenario with 100 smart meters show the proposed method requires only 10 s for encryption, significantly less than conventional methods. Clustering performance is excellent: valid and invalid data are clearly distinguished, the deviation between actual and computed cluster centers is small, and clustering accuracy reaches 89.54%. Furthermore, by integrating a Shamir (3,5) threshold secret sharing scheme and a redundancy strategy for fog node data storage, the method maintains continuous operation and data integrity despite server failures or meter data loss. The data recovery rate exceeds 98%, with less than 4% loss in clustering accuracy. These results demonstrate the method achieves efficient encryption, high clustering accuracy, and strong fault tolerance, effectively enhancing private information security in smart grids.
